children.text: sāndrodrekakṣubhitam abhitaḥ svāntam antar niyamya prāyo dhatte navanavarasollekham ānandakandam ||
children.translated_text: Having restrained within the mind that is everywhere agitated by dense upsurges, it generally assumes the root of bliss, marked by ever new flashes of fresh rasa.

children.text: bhūyo bhūyaḥ pralayavibhavoddāmaduḥkhāntarāyo yo 'sāv antar jayati hṛdaye ko 'pi saṃvidvikāsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again and again there triumphs in the heart some expansion of consciousness, whose interruption is the intense pain arising from the manifestation of dissolution.

children.text: iha khalu nikhilajagadātmā sarvottīrṇaś ca sarvamayaś ca vikalpāsaṃkucitasaṃvitprakāśarūpaḥ anavacchinnacidānandaviśrāntaḥ prasaradaviralavicitrapañcavāhavāhavāhinīmahodadhiḥ niratiśayasvātantryasīmani pragalbhamānaḥ sarvaśaktikhacita eka eva asti saṃvid ātmā maheśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here indeed there is one conscious self, <s>Maheśvara</s>: the self of the whole universe, transcending everything and consisting of everything, whose nature is the light of consciousness unconstricted by conceptual distinctions, resting in undivided consciousness and bliss, a great ocean in which the spreading, uninterrupted, variegated stream of the five currents flows, becoming bold at the limit of unsurpassed freedom, and endowed with all powers.

children.text: tasya prakāśarūpatā cicchaktiḥ svātantryam ānandaśaktiḥ taccamatkāraḥ icchāśaktiḥ āmarśātmakatā jñānaśaktiḥ sarvākārayogitvaṃ kriyāśaktiḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: His nature as light is the power of consciousness; his freedom is the power of bliss; his wonder at that is the power of will; his reflective self-awareness is the power of knowledge; and his union with all forms is the power of action.

children.text: itthaṃ sarvaśaktiyoge 'pi ābhir mukhyābhiḥ śaktibhir upacaryate sa ca bhagavān svātantryaśaktimahimnā svātmānaṃ saṃkucitam iva ābhāsayan aṇuḥ iti ucyate ||
children.translated_text: Thus, although he is joined with all powers, he is conventionally described through these chief powers; and that blessed one, by the greatness of his power of freedom, making his own self appear as if contracted, is called the individual soul.
As has been said:
For <s>Śiva</s> is all-pervasive; because of the sealing contraction made by his own will,
and because of the mass of actions with their various fruits, he assumes this or that body.

children.text: iti nijasvarūpagopanakelilolam evaṃ māheśaśaktiparispandaṃ pravaraguravaḥ pratipedire ||
children.translated_text: Thus the eminent teachers understood this vibration of the power of <s>Maheśa</s> as delighting in the play of concealing its own nature.
And so they say:
Because he accomplishes what is exceedingly difficult, from stainless independence,
the supreme Lord is skilled in the game of concealing his own self.
Even though his own nature is uncovered, the Lord's covering of himself
is itself ignorance, since difference, on which the whole operation of the universe rests, is just this much.
Thus.

children.text: na ca etāvatā bhagavato deśakālākāropādhivirahitaniratiśayānandaparispandātmakasya kācid api kṣatiḥ pratyuta paramamahimnaḥ paripuṣṭir ity uktam ||
children.translated_text: And by this there is no loss at all to the blessed one, whose nature is the unsurpassed vibration of bliss, free from the limiting adjuncts of place, time, and form; on the contrary, it is an enhancement of his supreme greatness, as has been said:
If <s>Maheśvara</s> were to remain with a body of a single form,
then, like a pot and the like, he would abandon both lordship and consciousness.
Limited luminosity is indeed the defining mark of the insentient.

children.text: jaḍād vilakṣaṇo bodho yato na parimīyate ||
children.translated_text: Awareness is distinct from the insentient, because it is not measured out.
Therefore the powers of the great ocean of awareness, rising up,
take on the variegated condition of collisions within themselves, like waves.
And so on.

children.text: tad evam asau bhagavān svamāyāśaktyākhyena avyabhicaritasvātantryaśaktimahimnā svātmanaiva ātmānaṃ saṃkucitam iva avabhāsayan vijñānākalaḥ pralayākalaḥ sakalaś ca sampadyate ||
children.translated_text: Thus that blessed one, by the greatness of the unfailing power of freedom called his own power of <s>māyā</s>, making himself by himself appear as if contracted, becomes the <s>vijñānākala</s>, the <s>pralayākala</s>, and the <s>sakala</s>.

children.text: tatra āṇavena ekenaiva malena saṃyukto vijñānākala ucyate dvābhyām āṇavamāyī yābhyām apavedyaḥ pralayākalaḥ tribhir āṇavamāyīyakārmaiḥ saṃvedyaḥ tair eva kalādidharaṇyantatattvamayaḥ sakalaḥ tadartham eva ayam arthasargaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Among these, one who is joined with the single impurity called <s>āṇava</s> is called a <s>vijñānākala</s>; one who is to be known through two impurities, <s>āṇava</s> and <s>māyīya</s>, is a <s>pralayākala</s>; and one who is to be known through three, <s>āṇava</s>, <s>māyīya</s>, and <s>kārma</s>, and who consists of the tattvas from <s>kalā</s> down to earth, is a <s>sakala</s>. For that very purpose there is this creation of objects.

children.text: tatra sṛṣṭyunmukho bhagavān śuddhādhvani vartamānaḥ svaśaktibhiḥ māyāṃ vikṣobhya kalātattvaṃ kiṃcitkartṛtvalakṣaṇaṃ pudgalasya sṛjati tato 'pi kiṃcid avabodhākhyaṃ vidyātattvaṃ kiṃcid abhilāṣarūpaṃ ca rāgatattvaṃ tad etat sarāgaṃ kartṛtattvaṃ bhūtabhaviṣyadvartamānatayā tridhā avacchidyate tat kālatattvaṃ tulyatve 'pi rāge yena kartṛtvasya avacchedaḥ kriyate tat niyatitattvaṃ tad etat kañcukaṣaṭkam antarmalāvṛtasya pudgalasya bahir ācchādakam uktaṃ ca cillācakreśvaramate māyā kalā śuddhavidyā rāgakālau niyantraṇā ||
children.translated_text: There, when the blessed one is turned toward creation and abides on the pure path, he agitates <s>māyā</s> with his powers and creates for the person the <s>kalā</s>-tattva, whose mark is a slight capacity for agency. From that he creates the <s>vidyā</s>-tattva, called a slight awareness, and also the <s>rāga</s>-tattva, whose form is a slight desire. This principle of agency together with desire is delimited threefold as past, future, and present: that is the <s>kāla</s>-tattva. That by which, even when desire is the same, the delimitation of agency is made is the <s>niyati</s>-tattva. This group of six coverings is said to be the outer covering of the person who is covered inwardly by impurity. And it is said in the doctrine of the lord of the wheel of consciousness: <s>māyā</s>, <s>kalā</s>, pure knowledge, <s>rāga</s>, the two times, and restriction
these six, because they cover, are the coverings of the limited self.
And thus the person's inner impurity is situated like a husk-like covering,
and the coverings are like chaff; therefore he is deprived of knowledge and action.
Thus.

children.text: sā ca kalā puruṣasya parimitaṃ kartṛtvaṃ prakāśya sukhaduḥkhamoharūpaṃ bhogyam avyaktatvaṃ sṛjati tato 'pi aṣṭaguṇaṃ buddhitattvam utpannaṃ tato 'pi sāttvikarājasatāmasabhedabhinnaṃ triskandham ahaṃkāratattvam tatra pūrvasmāt ahaṃkārāt mano jātam aparasmāt indriyāṇi tṛtīyāt tanmātrāṇi ebhyo bhūtāni ity evam ayam ekasyaiva ādidevasya svātantryamahimnā saṃsāre saṃsarataḥ parimitapramātṛtām avalambamānasya tattvaprasaraḥ uktaṃ ca bhūtāni tanmātragaṇendriyāṇi mūlaṃ pumān kañcukayuk suśuddham ||
children.translated_text: And that <s>kalā</s>, revealing the person's limited agency, creates the unmanifest object of enjoyment, whose forms are pleasure, pain, and delusion. From that is produced the intellect-tattva with its eight qualities; from that again the ego-tattva, divided by the distinctions of the sāttvika, rājasa, and tāmasa and having three branches. From the first ego arises the mind, from the next the sense faculties, and from the third the subtle elements; from these arise the gross elements. In this way there has been taught the expansion of tattvas of the one primal god, who, by the greatness of his freedom, moves through saṃsāra while assuming the state of a limited knower. And it has been said: The elements, the group of subtle elements and sense faculties, the root, the person joined with the coverings, and the very pure
up to the powers beginning with knowledge: this is the manifold spreading of waves from the ocean of his own consciousness.
Likewise:

children.text: saala utta puriṣuṇṇa u saallutta uttiṇṇa
children.translated_text: The <s>sakala</s>, moreover, is complete; the one beyond the <s>sakala</s> is transcendent.

children.text: pari āṇaha attāṇa u pari masiveṇa samāṇa u
children.translated_text: Yet know the self in the limited one as equal to <s>Maheśvara</s>.
Thus.

children.text: eteṣāṃ ca uktarūpāṇāṃ tattvānāṃ pramātṛbhede vaicitryāt prameyavaicitryaṃ bhavati iti śrīpūrvaśāstre kathitam tathā hi śaktimacchaktibhedena dharātattvaṃ vibhidyate ||
children.translated_text: And because, in these tattvas whose nature has been stated, there is variety in the object of knowledge owing to variety in the knower, this is taught in the <s>Śrīpūrvaśāstra</s>. Thus: the earth-tattva is divided according to the distinction between power-possessors and powers.
And that, together with its own nature, should be known as fifteenfold.
By this very procedure, from the <s>puṃs-tattva</s> up to the <s>kalā</s>,
it is to be known as thirteenfold; like <s>Rudra</s>, the <s>pralayākala</s>
is so, and <s>māyā</s> too is to be understood as ninefold; the <s>jñānakevala</s>
and the mantras are sevenfold in the same way; the lords of mantra are fivefold;

children.text: tridhā mantreśvareśānāḥ śivaḥ sākṣān na bhidyate ||
children.translated_text: the lords over the lord of mantras are threefold; <s>Śiva</s> himself is not divided.

children.text: yaḥ punaḥ sarvatattvāni vetty etāni yathārthataḥ
children.translated_text: But one who knows all these tattvas as they really are
is declared to be a guru equal to me, one who reveals the power of mantra.

children.text: dṛṣṭāḥ sambhāṣitās tena spṛṣṭāś ca prīticetasā
children.translated_text: Men who have been seen by him, spoken to by him,
and touched by him with a mind of affection are freed even from sins committed over seven births.
Thus.
Thus, then, this is the sequence of tattvas, having many determinations.

children.text: eteṣāṃ ca tattvānāṃ vargaśo yad anugāmi rūpam ekarūpam ekarūpakalanāsahiṣṇutvāt sā kalā kathyate ||
children.translated_text: And among these tattvas, the single form that follows each group as a class, because it is capable of construing them into one form, is called a <s>kalā</s>.

children.text: tathā hi nivartante yatas tattvavargāḥ sā nivṛttir nāma kalā ||
children.translated_text: Thus, that from which the groups of tattvas turn back is the kalā named <s>nivṛtti</s>.
And it is established in earth alone.

children.text: kāraṇatve pūraṇāpyāyakāritvāt pratiṣṭhā nāma kalā ucyate ||
children.translated_text: Because, as cause, it brings filling and nourishment, the kalā is called <s>pratiṣṭhā</s>.
And it is established pervading from water and the other elements up to the root.
When the knowable dissolves, because consciousness predominates, there is the kalā named <s>vidyā</s>.
And it occupies the path from <s>pumān</s> up to <s>māyā</s>.
Because the waves of the limiting sheaths subside, the kalā is called <s>śāntā</s>.
And it is situated from <s>śuddhavidyā</s> through <s>śakti</s>. Thus.
This very thing is the fourfold cosmic egg, characterized as earthy, prakritic, māyic, and śāktic.
Because it transcends all, in the <s>śiva-tattva</s> there is the kalā <s>śāntyatītā</s>, beyond peace.
Thus.

children.text: paraṃ tu tattvaṃ svatantratvāt kalātītam āsām eva kalānāṃ tattvavad antarbhūtāni bhuvanāny api boddhavyāni evaṃ sthūlasūkṣmaparatvena bhuvanatattvakalārūpaṃ trividharūpaṃ prameyam uktam pramāṇam api tathaiva padamantravarṇatayā trividham eva iti ekasyaiva pūrṇapramātuḥ svātantryāt saṃsarataḥ ṣaḍvidhe adhvani viśrāntir uktā ||
children.translated_text: But the supreme tattva, because it is independent, is beyond the kalās. The worlds too should be understood as included within these very kalās, just as the tattvas are. In this way the knowable has been stated to be threefold in form, as world, tattva, and kalā, according to gross, subtle, and supreme levels. The means of knowledge likewise is threefold, as word, mantra, and phoneme. Thus, because of the freedom of the one complete knower who transmigrates, repose within the sixfold path has been taught.

children.text: bhavanti cātra dīkṣāparighaṭanasaṃgrahaślokāḥ padamantravarṇam ekaṃ puraṣoḍaśakaṃ dhareti ca nivṛttiḥ ||
children.translated_text: And here there are summary verses on the arrangement of initiation: one word, mantra, and phoneme; the set of sixteen worlds; earth; this is <s>nivṛtti</s>.
The other kalā has the tattva and phoneme, fire and eye, the worlds called rasa and arrow, and the weapon-mantra word.
The further kalā has the sage-tattvas and phonemes, two words and mantras, and the worlds called Vasus and eyes.
The fourth has the fire-phonemes and tattva, one word and mantra, and one world together with it.

children.text: ṣoḍaśa varṇāḥ padamantratattvam ekaṃ ca śāntyatīteyam ||
children.translated_text: Sixteen phonemes, one word, mantra, and tattva: this is <s>śāntyatītā</s>.
Thus.

children.text: tad evam āṇavīṃ vṛttim ālambya bhagavān vicitraiḥ jātyāyurbhogaiḥ jarāyujāṇḍajodbhedajasvedajādijātaṃ prādurbhāvayati ||
children.translated_text: Thus, relying on the atomic mode of activity, the Lord brings forth beings born from womb, egg, sprout, sweat, and so on, with varied births, lifespans, and experiences.

children.text: tatra upabhuktasya annapānasya pākavaśāt rasarūpatayā sthitasya raktamāṃsamedo'sthimajjātmanā śukradhātau viśrāntir bhavati tatra imāḥ prajāḥ prajāyante ||
children.translated_text: There, food and drink that have been consumed, standing as rasa by the force of digestion, come to rest in the semen-dhātu through the forms of blood, flesh, fat, bone, and marrow. There these creatures are born.

children.text: tathā coktaṃ sauśrute iha khalu pāñcabhautikasya caturvidhasya āhārasya ṣaḍrasopetasya dvividharasavīryasya aṣṭavidharasavīryasya anekaprakāropabhuktasya pariṇatasya yas tejorūpaḥ sāraḥ sūkṣmaḥ sa rasa ity ucyate tasya hṛdayaṃ sthānaṃ sa ca hṛdayāt caturviṃśatidhamanīr anupraviśya ūrdhvagā daśa daśa ca adhogāminīḥ catasraḥ tiryaggāḥ sakalaṃ śarīram aharahas tarpayati jīvayati dhārayati vardhayati adṛṣṭanimittena karmaṇā sa khalu āpyo raso yakṛtplīhādiṃ prāpya rāgam upaiti bhavanti vā atra ślokāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And so it is said in the <s>Sauśruta</s>: Here, indeed, when fourfold food, made of the five elements, furnished with six tastes, having twofold rasa and potency, or eightfold rasa and potency, and consumed in many different ways, has been transformed, that subtle essence which is fiery in form is called <s>rasa</s>. Its place is the heart. From the heart it enters the twenty-four vessels: ten going upward, ten going downward, and four going crosswise. Day by day it satisfies, enlivens, supports, and increases the whole body through karma whose cause is unseen. That watery rasa, reaching the liver, spleen, and so forth, takes on redness. And there are verses here:

children.text: rañjitās tejasā tv āpaḥ śarīrasthena dehinām
children.translated_text: The waters in the bodies of embodied beings, colored by the bodily fire,

children.text: avyāpannāḥ prasannena raktam ity eva tad viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: when unvitiated and clear, are known precisely as blood.

children.text: rasād eva striyo raktaṃ rajaḥsaṃjñaṃ pravartate
children.translated_text: From rasa itself, in women, blood known as menstrual flow comes forth;

children.text: tadvaśād dvādaśād ūrdhvaṃ yāti pañcāśatiḥ kṣitim ||
children.translated_text: under its influence, after the twelfth year, it goes to decline at the fiftieth.
Menstrual fluid is blood, fiery in nature, because the embryo is both fiery and lunar.

children.text: rasād raktaṃ tato māṃsaṃ māṃsamedaś ca jāyate ||
children.translated_text: From rasa comes blood, from that flesh, and from flesh fat is produced.
From fat comes bone, then marrow, and from marrow arises semen.

children.text: evaṃ māṃsena śukratvaṃ raso yāti yathākramam
children.translated_text: In this way, through flesh and in due order, rasa reaches the state of semen;
and likewise in women, within a month, the arising of menstrual fluid occurs.
Thus.

children.text: tad evaṃbhūte mātṛpitṛsambandhasambhūte agnīṣomātmake raktaretasī kusumasamayād anantaraṃ jananījaṭhare retaḥ kalilībhavati tato budbudam tataḥ peśī tato ghanaḥ yāvad aṅgaparigrahaḥ aṅgavyaktiḥ saṃvidullāsaḥ sarvāṅgasampattir ojaḥsaṃcāraḥ sukhaduḥkhasaṃvittir iti yāvat prajāyate ||
children.translated_text: In such blood and semen, born from the relation of mother and father and made of fire and soma, after the time of menstruation, the semen becomes a coagulum in the mother's womb. From that comes a bubble, then a lump of flesh, then a solid mass, and so on until the assumption of limbs, the manifestation of limbs, the flash of consciousness, the completion of all limbs, the circulation of vital essence, and the awareness of pleasure and pain, up to the point of birth.
It is said in the doctrine of <s>Śrīcillācakreśvara</s>:
From the expansion of the essences of moon and sun and their mutual friction,
when the fire has arisen and the middle abode has opened,
through the transformation into heroic redness, the sprout comes into being.
Semen that has remained for one night, when emitted, becomes a coagulum;
after seven nights it becomes a bubble; after a month a lump of flesh is produced.
In the second month it becomes a solid mass, and in the third it assumes fire.
In the fourth month there is consciousness for those whose limbs have become manifest; in the fifth it comes to be.
In the sixth there is the joining together of all the limbs; in the seventh the arising of movement.
In the eighth month heat moves through it; in the ninth there is sensation.
In the tenth month the creature, its body complete, is born.
When born, touched by the wind and pressed by the mechanism of the womb,
it does not remember the fierce torment produced by many births.
Gradually these causes of its body come to growth.

children.text: rasaḥ sthitiṃ prakurute raktaṃ saṃjīvayaty alam
children.translated_text: Rasa establishes stability; blood fully gives life.

children.text: māṃsaṃ bṛṃhayati prāyo medaḥ snehayati sphuṭam ||
children.translated_text: Flesh generally nourishes; fat clearly anoints and moistens.
The bones support it, and marrow rests within as the inner essence.
Semen produces delight and increase; urine separates moisture.
Feces is said to block wind and fire.
Sweat is the instrument of moisture, and menstrual blood is the cause of conception.
Having thus obtained a body composed of six sheaths through its appropriation,

children.text: anapekṣya nijaṃ bhāvaṃ pumān bhāvān apekṣate ||
children.translated_text: a person, disregarding his own true state, depends upon external states.
Thus.

children.text: ayam eva ca artho niruktikṛtāpi uktapārthivān aṣṭau guṇān vidyāt trīn mātṛtaḥ trīn pitṛtaḥ ityādy upakramya uktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And this very meaning has also been stated by the author of the Nirukti, beginning with, 'one should know eight earthy qualities: three from the mother, three from the father,' and so on.

children.text: atraiva idaṃ puṃstrīnapuṃsakalakṣaṇaṃ prakṛtitrayakāraṇam somādhikyena puṃjanma sūryādhikyena yoṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here too this mark of male, female, and neuter, whose cause is the threefold constitution, is taught: because of an excess of Soma there is male birth; because of an excess of the Sun there are females.

children.text: sāmyāt klības tu vātena bhedāt syād bahvapatyatā ||
children.translated_text: From equality there is a neuter; and through wind, from division, there may be much offspring.
Thus.

children.text: avayavabhedo 'pi navame daśame māsi prabalaiḥ sūtimārutaiḥ
children.translated_text: The division of the limbs too: in the ninth or tenth month, by the powerful winds of delivery,
it is expelled, feverish, like an arrow through the hole of a machine.

children.text: tasya ṣoḍhā śarīraṃ tatṣaṭtvaco dhārayanti ca
children.translated_text: Its body is sixfold, and six skins hold it together.
Of bones, three hundred plus sixty are bound together.

children.text: sthūlaiḥ saha catuḥṣaṣṭir daśanā viṃśatir nakhāḥ
children.translated_text: Together with the large ones there are sixty-four; the teeth are twenty, and the nails twenty.
The rods of the hands and feet, and four sets in their places,

children.text: ṣaṣṭyaṅgulīnāṃ dve pārṣṇī gulpheṣu ca catuṣṭayam
children.translated_text: two heels among the sixty fingers and toes, and four in the ankles,

children.text: catvāry aratnikāsthīni jaṅghayos tāvad eva tu ||
children.translated_text: four forearm bones, and just as many in the shanks.
Two each are to be specified as arising in the knees, cheeks, thighs, shoulder-blades, and shoulders,
and in the eye-sockets and in the pelvic plates.

children.text: bhagāsthy ekaṃ tathā pṛṣṭhe catvāriṃśac ca pañca ca
children.translated_text: There is one pubic bone, and in the back forty-five bones.

children.text: grīvā pañcadaśāsthīni jatrv ekaṃ ca tathā hanuḥ ||
children.translated_text: There are fifteen bones in the neck, one collarbone, and likewise the jaw.
At its root are two, and the dense bones of the forehead, eyes, cheeks, and nose.

children.text: parśukās talakaiḥ sārdham arbude ca dvisaptatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The ribs, together with the palatal bones and the arbuda bones, are seventy-two.

children.text: dvau śaṅkhakau kapālāni catvāry eva śiras tathā
children.translated_text: There are two temple bones, and exactly four skull bones in the head.
There are fifteen bones in the chest: this is the collection of a person's bones.
Thus.
Among these very bones, other treatises state names according to the distinctions kapāla, bharaṇa, turuṇḍa, ruṇḍa, rucaka, nala, yaṣṭīla, nalaka, and so forth.
He states the other locations.
The fat, the omentum, the killing organ, the navel, kloman, liver, and spleen,
the small intestine, kidneys, bladder, feces, and apāna,

children.text: āmāśayo 'tha hṛdayaṃ sthūlāntraṃ gudam eva ca ||
children.translated_text: the stomach, then the heart, the large intestine, and the anus,

children.text: uttarau ca gudau koṣṭhau vistāro 'yam udāhṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: and the two upper rectal chambers: this is declared to be the extent of the belly.
The pupils, the eye-corners, the ear-shells, and the ear-lobes,
the cheeks, temples, eyebrows, the two painful encasements, the lips, and the hollows at the loins,
the groins, testicles, kidneys, the two accumulations of phlegm, and the breasts,
the sublingual parts, the buttocks, the tongue, the shanks, and the thighs and calves,
the palate, belly, head of the bladder, chin, throat, and uvula,
the four sets of eyelashes, and the feet, hands, and heart,
the hollow at the throat and other such places are locations in this body.
Those same nine openings are also the abodes of vital breath.

children.text: dhamanīnāṃ śate dve tu pañcapeśīśatāni ca ||
children.translated_text: There are two hundred arteries and five hundred muscles.
Thus.

children.text: strīṇāṃ ca stanayor gartād aṣṭātriṃśadadhikāḥ sapeśyo dhamanyo bhavanti iti sauśrutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And for women, from the hollows of the two breasts onward, there are thirty-eight additional vessels with muscles, according to the Suśruta tradition.
There are twenty-nine lakhs and nine hundred sinews,
and the series of veins and arteries should be known as fifty-six.

children.text: saptottaraṃ marmaśataṃ dve tu saṃdhiśate tathā
children.translated_text: There are one hundred and seven vital spots, and likewise two hundred joints.

children.text: lomnāṃ koṭyas tu pañcāśaccatasraḥ koṭya eva ca ||
children.translated_text: The hairs are fifty-four crores in number.
There are known to be nine añjalis of rasa and ten of water.

children.text: sapta vai tu purīṣasya raktasyāṣṭau prakīrtitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Seven are stated for feces and eight for blood.

children.text: śleṣmā ṣaṭ pañca pittaṃ ca catvāro mūtram eva ca
children.translated_text: Phlegm is six, bile is five, and urine is four.

children.text: vasātrayaṃ ca dvau medo majjaikārdhaṃ ca mastake ||
children.translated_text: Fat is three, adipose tissue two, and marrow one half in the head.

children.text: śleṣmaujasas tāvad eva retasas tāvad eva ca
children.translated_text: Ojas mixed with phlegm is just as much, and semen is just as much.

children.text: ity etad asthiraṃ varṣma yasya mokṣāya kṛty asau ||
children.translated_text: Such is this unstable body, for whose liberation one should act.
Thus, for a healthy person of gentle humoral constitution, it is so.

children.text: anyathā tu vailakṣaṇyāc charīrāṇām asvasthatvāt tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: But otherwise, because bodies differ and because they are likewise unhealthy,
there is no fixed measure of the doṣas, tissues, and wastes.
So it has been said.

children.text: tad etat vibhāgena bībhatsadarśanaṃ vairāgyamunibhir agāyi tathā cāhuḥ
children.translated_text: This, when divided out, has been sung by sages of detachment as a disgusting sight. And they say:
It has bones as its pillars, is bound with sinews, and is smeared with flesh and blood.
Covered with skin, foul-smelling, and filled with urine and feces,
pervaded by old age and grief, a seat of disease, afflicted,

children.text: rajasvalam anityaṃ ca bhūtāvāsam imaṃ tyajet ||
children.translated_text: menstruous and impermanent, this dwelling of beings should be abandoned.
The sage <s>Pārāśarya</s> also says:
For the sake even of a little body, which is the storehouse of every impurity, ungrateful, and perishable,
fools commit sins.
For the body that is gradually being sustained by foods, with difficulty, for the sake of pleasure,

children.text: ko hi nāma śarīrāya dharmāpetaṃ samācaret
children.translated_text: who indeed would perform an act devoid of <s>dharma</s> for the sake of the body?
Thus.

children.text: evaṃ śarīram uktvā śarīrisvarūpam ucyate dvāsaptatisahasrāṇi hṛdayād abhiniḥsṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having thus described the body, the nature of the embodied one is now described: seventy-two thousand channels issue forth from the heart.

children.text: hitā nāmāhitā nāḍyas tāsāṃ madhye śaśiprabham ||
children.translated_text: They are called beneficial and harmful nāḍīs; in their midst is a moon-bright disk.

children.text: maṇḍalaṃ tasya madhyastha ātmā dīpa ivācalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the middle of that stands the self, unmoving like a lamp.

children.text: sa jñeyas taṃ viditveha punar ājāyate na tu ||
children.translated_text: He is to be known; having known him here, one is not born again.

children.text: idam atra tātparyaṃ taṃ tathābhūtam ātmānaṃ viditvā naro na janmakleśam anubhavati kiṃbhūtaṃ yaddhṛdayoktaṃ dvāsaptatisaṃkhyāvacchinnaṃ nāḍīcakraṃ tadantar yat śaśimaṇḍalaṃ tadantaḥsthaṃ tāś ca nāḍyo 'śitapītarasasaṃcaraṇādhikāratvāt puṇyopacayena hitāḥ tadabhāvena ahitāḥ tāsāṃ saṃcāraka eka eva vyavahārabhedāt pañcabhedo vāyuḥ tāsāṃ ca dve pradhāne dakṣiṇottarasambaddhe agnīṣomātmake taddvāreṇa prāṇasya ūrdhvagamanam ahaḥ adho 'pānasya rātriḥ etena ardhamāsamāsartuvatsarādikālavibhāgo 'pi vyākhyātaḥ samaprāṇacāro viṣuvat tayor madhye tṛtīyā daṇḍākārā brahmanāḍī sthitā tatra niruddhaprāṇo yogī dīpākāram ātmānaṃ paśyati iti ata evoktaṃ samyagdarśanasampannaḥ karmabhir na sa badhyate ||
children.translated_text: The purport here is this: having known the self as being such, a person does not undergo the suffering of birth. What is it like? Within the wheel of nāḍīs mentioned in the heart and delimited by the number seventy-two thousand, there is the lunar disk, and the self stands within that. Those nāḍīs, because they have the function of circulating the essence of what has been eaten and drunk, are beneficial when there is an accumulation of merit, and harmful in its absence. The one mover through them, or by distinction of function fivefold, is the wind. Of those, two are chief, connected with the right and the left, having the nature of fire and soma. Through them there is the upward movement of prāṇa by day and the downward movement of apāna by night. By this the division of time into fortnights, months, seasons, years, and so on is also explained. The equal course of the breaths is the equinox. Between those two stands a third, staff-shaped <s>brahmanāḍī</s>. There, with prāṇa restrained, the yogin sees the self in the form of a lamp. Therefore it has been said: one endowed with true vision is not bound by actions.
But one who is devoid of vision enters <s>saṃsāra</s>.
Thus.

children.text: saṃsārapravṛttau ca tasya kalāto viṣayavibhedo munibhir uktaḥ tathā hi
children.translated_text: And when <s>saṃsāra</s> proceeds, the sages have described the differentiation of his objects according to <s>kalā</s>. Thus:
One who covets others' property, and likewise thinks of what is undesirable,
and who clings to false notions, is born in the lowest wombs.
A man who speaks untruth, and likewise a man who is slanderous,
and one who babbles incoherently, is born among beasts and birds.
One who is devoted to taking what has not been given, and one who approaches another's wife,
and one who injures contrary to rule, is born among immobile beings.

children.text: ityādi ayaṃ tu uktayātanasya niyogaḥ advayarūpasya ātmanaḥ kutastyo 'yaṃ bhedaḥ iti cet māyāmahāmohavikalpakalpita ity āha ākāśam ekaṃ hi yathā ghaṭādiṣu pṛthag bhavet ||
children.translated_text: And so on. But this is only the assignment of the torments described. If it is asked, 'Whence is this difference in the self, whose nature is nondual?', he says that it is fashioned by the constructs of the great delusion of <s>māyā</s>: just as one single space appears separate in pots and the like,
so too the self, though one, is many, like the sun in vessels of water.
Thus.

children.text: na ca apakvakaṣāyasya kadācid api uktarūpam ātmajñānaṃ bhavati tathā ca malino hi yathādarśo rūpālokasya na kṣamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And one whose impurities are unripe never has self-knowledge of the form described. Thus: just as a soiled mirror is not capable of showing the appearance of a form,

children.text: tathā hy apakvakaraṇa ātmajñānasya na kṣamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: so one whose instruments are unripe is not capable of self-knowledge.
So it has been said, and so on.
Enough, then, with saying more.

children.text: evam asau bhagavān svātantryaśaktimahimnā paśudaśām avalambamāno bhogopadānapravaṇaḥ sampūrṇadehaprāṇabalaḥ san uktena ṣaḍadhvajālakrameṇa prabuddhaḥ śarīraparigraham āsādayati krameṇa bhukteṣu karmasu ṣaḍbhir bhāvavikārair jarārogādibhiḥ kāyayantre vighaṭamāne dehastambho vepathur nāḍīcakrasaṃkocaḥ kvacid viparyayeṇa tadvikāso marmabhaṅgaḥ śoṣa ityādi pūrvasaṃsthāpanopamardakaṃ sarvam upapadyate yāvat vinaśyati vināśaś ca kṣaṇiko 'sya yady api tathāpi sthūlayā vṛttyā daśabhir daśabhir abhivyaktaḥ proktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus that blessed one, by the greatness of his power of freedom, assuming the condition of the bound soul and inclined toward the presentation of enjoyments, endowed with a complete body, breath, and strength, is awakened according to the sequence of the net of the six paths described and obtains embodiment. As actions are gradually experienced, when the bodily machine is breaking down through the six transformations of being, old age, disease, and the like, everything that oppresses the previous constitution comes about: rigidity of the body, trembling, contraction of the wheel of nāḍīs, sometimes its expansion in the opposite condition, breaking of the vital points, wasting, and so on, until it perishes. And although its destruction is momentary, nevertheless, from a gross point of view, it is said to become manifest decade by decade.

children.text: tathā hi bālyaṃ vṛddhir balaṃ prajñā tvak cakṣuḥ śrotram indriyam ||
children.translated_text: Thus: childhood, growth, strength, understanding, skin, eye, ear, faculty,

children.text: āsanaṃ śayanaṃ puṃsāṃ daśabhir daśabhir vrajet ||
children.translated_text: sitting, and lying down pass for human beings decade by decade.
So it has been said.

children.text: tataś ca tasmin śarīrayantre vighaṭite sā saṃvit prāṇanātmatām avalambya ātivāhikena dehena dehāntaraṃ nīyate tataś ca ātivāhikaṃ śarīrakaṃ bhūtabhaviṣyaddehāntarāle yugyasthānīyaṃ sambhavati yadārūḍho 'sau pudgalaḥ śarīrāntarāsaṅgam anubhavati uktaṃ ca kośabhāṣye mṛtyūpapattibhavayor antarā bhavatīha yaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And then, when that bodily machine has broken down, that consciousness, taking on the nature of prāṇa, is carried by an intermediate body to another body. Thus the intermediate body exists between the past body and the future body, in the position of a yoke; mounted upon it, that person experiences contact with another body. And it is said in the <s>Kośabhāṣya</s>: That which exists here between the states of death and rebirth
is established as the intermediate existence, because it is attached to the place to be reached.
It arises in a delimited way, by similarity with a continuum of rice grains.
Because a reflection is not established, and because the example is dissimilar,
it exists after the moment of death and before the moment of rebirth,
possessing discernment of actions visible to the pure faculties of its own kind and of pure action.
Thus.

children.text: śrutiś ca dve te cakre sūrye brahmāṇa ṛtuthā viduḥ
children.translated_text: And scripture says: 'Those two wheels, O Sun, the knowers of <s>brahman</s> know season by season;

children.text: athaikaṃ cakraṃ yad guhā tad addhātaya id viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: but the one wheel that is in the cave, only those who are grounded in truth know.'

children.text: iti ayam arthaḥ he sūrye bhagavati ātmaśakte brahmāṇaḥ brahmavādinaḥ ṛtuthā kāle kāle te tava sambandhinī dve cakre viduḥ cakram iva cakraṃ parivartasādharmyāt śarīram ucyate tayor dvitvaṃ vartamānabhāvibhedāt atas tayor antare kathitayā yuktyā yad ekam ātivāhikākhyaṃ tat guhā guptam anupalakṣyam ity arthaḥ ata eva tad addhātayaḥ it viduḥ yogina eva jānanti iti tātparyam ||
children.translated_text: Thus the meaning is this: O Sun, blessed power of the self, the knowers of <s>brahman</s>, the speakers of <s>brahman</s>, know at each proper time the two wheels belonging to you. It is called a wheel because, like a wheel, it turns; the body is meant. Their duality is due to the distinction between the present and the future. Therefore, between those two, by the reasoning already stated, there is one body called intermediate; it is in the cave, that is, hidden and not perceived. For that very reason only those grounded in truth know it: the purport is that only yogins know it.

children.text: tathā ca jāgradavasthāyāṃ dṛḍhakaraṇasya pramātur indriyāṇi śrotrādīni śabdādayaś ca viṣayā bhavanti tathā prameyasamaye pracalitam antaḥkaraṇam indriyaṃ yiyāsutā ca viṣayaḥ tām eva yiyāsutām adhikṛtya pravaramuniḥ pārāśaryaḥ samādhitavān
children.translated_text: And just as, in the waking state, for the firmly constituted knower the senses such as hearing and the objects such as sound are the domains, so too, at the time of what is to be known, the moving inner organ is the sense-organ and the desire to go is the object. It is precisely with reference to that desire to go that the excellent sage <s>Pārāśarya</s> composed the verse:

children.text: yaṃ yaṃ vāpi smaran bhāvaṃ tyajaty ante kalevaram
children.translated_text: Whatever state a person remembers when at the end he gives up the body,

children.text: taṃ tam evaiti kaunteya sadā tadbhāvabhāvitaḥ
children.translated_text: that very state he reaches, O <s>Kaunteya</s>, being always formed by that state.
Thus.

children.text: ayam atra saṃkṣepārthaḥ sambhavabhogaḥ janmabhogaḥ sthitibhogaś ca iti tisraḥ śarīrasya prāgavasthā bhavanti hi tathā hi jaṭhare cetanāyāṃ saṃjātāyāṃ garbhabhogaḥ prasavasamaye janmabhogaḥ prasūtasya bālyādivayaḥparāvṛttyā vicitraḥ sthitibhogaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The concise meaning here is this: the enjoyment of origination, the enjoyment of birth, and the enjoyment of continued existence are the three prior states of the body. Thus, when consciousness has arisen in the womb, there is the enjoyment of the embryo; at the time of delivery there is the enjoyment of birth; and for one who has been born, through the transformation of ages beginning with childhood, there is the manifold enjoyment of continued existence.

children.text: mṛtibhogaḥ yiyāsutā ca dve caramāvasthe tatra mṛtibhogaḥ vicitrā śarīrapīḍā yiyāsutā ātivāhikaśarīrasambaddhā tām eva ca yiyāsutām uddiśya yaṃ yaṃ vāpi smaran bhāvam ||
children.translated_text: The enjoyment of death and the desire to go are the two final states. Among these, the enjoyment of death is the varied pain of the body. The desire to go is connected with the <s>ātivāhika</s> body, the transitive body; and it is precisely with regard to that desire to go that the passage beginning "whatever state he remembers" proceeds.

children.text: ityādi pravṛttam ata eva bhūtabhaviṣyadarthahitārthavādinaḥ smarann iti śabdapratyayasya yathārthaḥ prayogaḥ syāt etad eva ca vitatya śrītantrāloke pratipāditam
children.translated_text: Therefore the use of the word-form "remembering" is literal, since it speaks for the welfare of past and future matters. And this very point has been set forth at length in the venerable <s>Tantrāloka</s>:
This whole experience of death cuts the vital points and brings stupefaction and loss of the senses.
There the senses are bewildered, and one is surrounded by the distress of breathing.

children.text: yas tv asau kṣaṇa evaikaś caramaḥ prāṇanātmakaḥ
children.translated_text: But that single final moment, whose nature is the life-breath,
is the small portion of the time of abandoning the body, separated from the vital breath.
In that moment, whatever one remembers through the awakening of former impressions,
that very form one attains, confused by pleasure and pain.
Thus.

children.text: atra ca viṣayanaiyatyena vibhāgo vyāsamuninaiva kṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: And here the division according to the fixity of the object has been made by the sage <s>Vyāsa</s> himself,

children.text: yadā sattve vivṛddhe tu pralayaṃ yāti dehabhṛt
children.translated_text: in the passage beginning, "When the embodied one goes to dissolution while sattva has increased,"
and so on.

children.text: tā etāḥ śarīrāvasthāḥ pañcāre cakre parivartamāne tasminn ātasthur bhuvanāni viśvā ||
children.translated_text: These bodily states are spoken of in the śruti passage, "The five-spoked wheel, when revolving, on it all the worlds stood,"
and so forth.
Elsewhere also it is said:

children.text: sambhavo janma sattā ca mṛtiś cātha yiyāsutā
children.translated_text: Origination, birth, existence, death, and then the desire to go:
these are the five transformations and reversals of the body.
Thus.

children.text: etad evam uktarūpeṇa asau ātivāhikena dehena dehāntaraṃ nīyate so 'pi dehaḥ suptotthitāt prabodham avāpya prāṇiti uktena cakreṇa so 'pi vinaśyati yāvat araghaṭṭaghaṭīyantravat parivartamāno 'ṇuḥ nānākāyanikāyaiḥ saṃsarati saṃsāre ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the manner stated, that self is led by the <s>ātivāhika</s> body to another body. That body too, having gained awakening like one risen from sleep, breathes; and by the cycle described, it too perishes. Thus the <s>aṇu</s>, the limited soul, revolves like the buckets of a water-wheel and transmigrates in saṃsāra through many classes of bodies.

children.text: tathā ca śrutiḥ sasyam iva martyaḥ pacyate sasyam iva jāyate punaḥ
children.translated_text: And so the śruti says, "A mortal ripens like grain; like grain he is born again."
Thus.
This has also been stated by the sage <s>Vyāsa</s> in the passage beginning, "Just as a man, casting off worn-out garments,"
and so forth.

children.text: atha kadācit parameśvarānugrahaśaktipātapavitritaḥ kenāpi dīkṣādinā upāyena saṃvidānandaviśrāntam advayaṃ nijaṃ rūpaṃ parāmṛśati tataḥ svarūpam ālambate yathoktaṃ śrīmālinīvijaye evam asyātmanaḥ kāle kasmiṃścid yogyatāvaśāt ||
children.translated_text: Now at some time, purified by the descent of the power of the grace of the supreme Lord, through some means such as initiation, he touches his own nondual nature, resting in the bliss of consciousness; then he takes hold of his true form. As is stated in the venerable <s>Mālinīvijaya</s>, beginning, "Thus, for this self, at some time, by force of fitness,"

children.text: ity upakramya tatkṣaṇād vopabhogād vā dehapāte śivaṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: and ending with the passage, "either at that very moment, or after enjoyment, at the fall of the body, he goes to <s>Śiva</s>."
Thus by that text ending in this way.

children.text: yad vā kvāpi parameśvarāyatane śarīram ativāhya pūrve vidhau krameṇa parameśvarībhavati tad uktaṃ śrīsāttvatāyām
children.translated_text: Or, having passed the body in some sanctuary of the supreme Lord, in the former procedure he gradually becomes one with the supreme Lord. This is stated in the venerable <s>Sāttvatā</s>:
Where, from the region of the palace doorway, the sound of the conch travels,

children.text: prayāti sarvato dikṣu tat kṣetraṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ matam ||
children.translated_text: going in all directions, that field is regarded as <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>.
That same place is proclaimed to be twice as effective when it is established by sages;

children.text: siddhāvatāritād devāt tad eva triguṇaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: and that same place is remembered as threefold when it comes from a deity manifested by perfected beings.
From one self-manifest, fourfold fruit, preceded by union,

children.text: phalaṃ sāyujyatāpūrvaṃ vijñeyaṃ tu kramāt tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: is to be understood in sequence for those whose minds are cultivated at the end of the body.
The mind of human beings, driven by impurity because of the power of corrupt senses,
at the time of death becomes purified in the temple of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
Thus.
In the venerable <s>Amṛteśaśikhā</s> also:
Those who die in the homes of those into whom the tattvas have descended,
who follow the command of <s>Śaṃkara</s>, in places of self-born beings, sages, gods, seers, humans, and so on,

children.text: mṛtās te tatpuraṃ prāpya pureśair dīkṣitāḥ kramāt
children.translated_text: having reached that city, are initiated in order by the lords of the city;

children.text: martye 'vatīrya vā nāvā prayānti paramaṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: or, descending to the mortal world by boat, they go to the supreme state.
There the self-born ones are twofold: some are intent on grace,
and some have come for their own purpose; the former bestow liberation.
Thus.

children.text: tatrāpi na sarvasya mokṣa ity uktam
children.translated_text: Even there, it has been stated that liberation is not for everyone:
For one who is merely a bound soul there is dwelling in the same world; for one who is initiated, nearness;

children.text: tatparasya tu sāyujyam ity ājñā pārameśvarī ||
children.translated_text: but for one devoted to that, union: such is the supreme Lord's command.

children.text: yas tūrdhvaśāstragas tatra tyaktāsthaḥ saṃśayena saḥ
children.translated_text: But one who follows a higher scripture there, having abandoned faith through doubt,

children.text: vrajed āyatanaṃ naiva sa phalaṃ kiṃcid aśnute ||
children.translated_text: does not go to the sanctuary and enjoys no fruit at all.
Those who in mind hate initiation, sacred places, and knowledge,

children.text: ācaranti ca tat te vai sarve nirayagāminaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and yet act accordingly, all of them go to hell.

children.text: ye ca svabhyastavijñānamayāḥ śivamayā hi te
children.translated_text: And those who are made of knowledge well practiced by themselves are indeed made of <s>Śiva</s>;

children.text: jīvanmuktā na teṣāṃ syān mṛtau kāpi vicāraṇā
children.translated_text: they are liberated while living, and for them there will be no deliberation at death.
Thus.
For this very reason it is said in the venerable <s>Niśāṭana</s>:

children.text: godoham iṣupātaṃ vā nayanonmīlanaṃ ca vā
children.translated_text: The milking of a cow, the flight of an arrow, or the opening of the eyes

children.text: samyagyuktaḥ pare tattve na bhūyo janmabhāg bhavet ||
children.translated_text: When properly joined to the supreme reality, he will not again become a partaker of birth.

children.text: yasmāt pūrvaṃ pare nyasto yenātmā brahmaṇi svayam
children.translated_text: Since previously, by him himself, the self has been placed in the supreme, in <s>brahman</s>.

children.text: smaraṇaṃ tu kathaṃ tasya prāṇānte samupasthite
children.translated_text: But how could there be remembrance of that for him when the end of the vital breaths has arrived?
Thus.
Also in the venerable <s>Rāmabhaṭṭāraka</s>, to this extent:

children.text: kṣetraṃ tathā tīrthaṃ yāvad brahmaṇi no viśet
children.translated_text: A sacred field and likewise a ford are relevant only so long as one has not entered into <s>brahman</s>.

children.text: tad viditvā śvapāko 'pi matsamo nātra saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: Having known that, even a dog-cooker is equal to me; there is no doubt about this.
Thus.
Also by the blessed lord of serpents:

children.text: tīrthe śvapacagṛhe vā naṣṭasmṛtir api parityajan deham
children.translated_text: At a sacred ford or in the house of a dog-cooker, even if his memory is lost as he abandons the body,
liberated at the very time of knowledge, free from slain sorrow, he goes to isolation.
Thus.
It is also said in the venerable <s>Pauṣkara</s>:
Established as the divinity of the principles down to earth,
a knower of mantra, a devotee of the Lord, faithful and always believing,
in whatever hermitage he may dwell, with his senses restrained,
he should constantly remember his own mantra residing in his own body, having installed its form there.
But at the time of renouncing the body, at rest wherever he may be,

children.text: prayāti padam ādyaṃ vai samutkrāntaḥ svavigraham
children.translated_text: having departed from his own body, he goes indeed to the primordial state.
Thus.
Elsewhere too:
The body itself is the sanctuary; one should not go to another sanctuary.

children.text: tīrtham ekaṃ śrayen mantram anyatīrthāni varjayet
children.translated_text: One should resort to the single ford, the mantra, and abandon other fords.
Thus.
Likewise:

children.text: svasthaceṣṭāś ca ye martyāḥ smaranti mama nārada
children.translated_text: Those mortals who remember me, O <s>Nārada</s>, while their faculties are healthy,
I remember them at the final time, even when they are like wood or stone.
So it is said.

children.text: na ca saṃsthitasya uttamatayā adhikāriṇo lokayātrāprasiddhāsruvimocanādiparidevitaṃ kāryam yathoktaṃ śrīpūrvaśāsane niṣiddhaṃ sarvaśāstrāṇāṃ rodanaṃ kāyaśāsanam ||
children.translated_text: And for the established practitioner, qualified in the highest way, lamentation such as the shedding of tears and wailing, known from worldly conduct, should not be performed. As stated in the venerable <s>Pūrvaśāsana</s>: weeping, bodily chastisement, is forbidden in all scriptures.
Especially in the <s>Bhairava Tantra</s>, noisy lamentation is imagined for bound souls.

children.text: ayuktam imam ācāraṃ tyajed vai naurdhvadaihikam
children.translated_text: One should abandon this improper custom, and not perform the post-funeral bodily rite.
Thus.

children.text: śrīmatarahasyatilake 'pi uttamanayādhikāriṇāṃ saṃvṛtanijasadācārāṇāṃ lokaprasiddhirakṣāyai tadācārāparityāgo 'pi āmnātaḥ tathā hi lokācārasya vicchedo na kartavyaḥ kadācana ||
children.translated_text: In the venerable <s>Rahasyatilaka</s> too, for those qualified for the highest path, who conceal their own true conduct, even the non-abandonment of that customary conduct is taught for preserving worldly reputation. For thus: the interruption of social custom should never be made.

children.text: guhyaṃ guhyataraṃ kāryaṃ bāhyaṃ bāhyāntaraṃ tathā iti ||
children.translated_text: What is secret, more secret, should be done; what is external, and what is both external and internal, likewise. Thus.

children.text: anayoś ca pakṣayor ekatarapakṣāvalambane pravaragurava eva pramāṇam ||
children.translated_text: And in the adoption of either one of these two positions, the foremost gurus alone are the authority.

children.text: pitruddeśena ca yāgajapahomopavāsādi gurum ārādhya avaśyaṃ vidhātavyam ity uktam śrīmahākule
children.translated_text: And for the sake of one's father, sacrifices, recitations, oblations, fasts, and the like must certainly be performed after propitiating the guru. It is said in the venerable <s>Mahākula</s>:
When the thread has been laid out, when the portion has been lost, and when it is furnished with whatever dust is desired,
even without summoning the mantra, in the ritually enjoined maṇḍala,
seven crores of mantras create their presence there.
How much more so the <s>Kaula</s> tradition, when summoned there and worshipped?
When this is directed toward the fathers, O auspicious one, it serves for their endless benefit.
Thus.
It is also said in the venerable <s>Pracaṇḍabhairava</s>:
Those mortals who have little body-strength and wealth, yet are devoted to the guru and mantra,
and are especially unable to perform the worship of the great sacrifice,

children.text: siddhaliṅgaṃ tadā teṣāṃ pitrarthaṃ pūjayed budhaḥ
children.translated_text: then a wise person should worship the perfected liṅga for the sake of their fathers.

children.text: ucitaṃ pūjanaṃ tatra devānām api durlabham ||
children.translated_text: The proper worship there is difficult even for the gods to obtain.

children.text: kulāny uddharate tatra daśa pūrvāparāṇy api
children.translated_text: There he uplifts ten families, both before and after.
Thus.
Also in the venerable <s>Bhāgeśamata</s>:
By poison, snakes, fire, epilepsy, hunger, overeating, and bondage,
by caṇḍālas, water, lightning, royal punishment, and thieves,
by heat, cold, carts, spiders, cold afflictions, and great herds,
by brahmins, mlecchas, heretics, uprooting, and violent procedures,

children.text: ye hatāḥ pāpakarmāṇo mitradroharatāś ca ye
children.translated_text: those sinners who have been killed, and those devoted to betraying friends,
and others who have betrayed their master, and those who have destroyed themselves,

children.text: gurviṇyo duścaritrāś ca prasavena hatāś ca yāḥ
children.translated_text: pregnant women of bad conduct, and those who have been killed in childbirth,
for them, O most excellent lady, there is no means of uplifting other than

children.text: vinā yāgaṃ vinā homaṃ vinā mūrtiparigraham
children.translated_text: a rite without sacrifice, without oblation, without taking hold of an image,
without a material body brought by the application of the great-net procedure,
namely the initiation called the uplifting of the dead, extending through all paths.
Thus.
That, then, is the procedure for those who follow the upper teaching.

children.text: itareṣāṃ tu svaśāstrasamayopanyastānuṣṭhānam eva śreyaḥ tad alam anena ||
children.translated_text: But for others, the performance laid down by the rule of their own scripture alone is best. Enough of this.

children.text: evaṃ samanantarodīritayā nītyā janmamaraṇaprabandhasambandham avadhārya akṛtrimasvarūpaparāmarśanena jīvanmuktim āsādya kṛtakṛtyatām ālambante santaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, having ascertained the relation of the course of birth and death by the method just stated, good people attain liberation while living through the recognition of their unconstructed nature, and take hold of having accomplished what was to be done.
As it is said:
You who have known the highest reality, from the ocean of consciousness, produced by the pressing extraction of the firm power of the heart,

children.text: amṛtam iti nigīrṇe kālakūṭe 'pi devā yadi pibata tadānīṃ niścitaṃ vaḥ śivatvam
children.translated_text: if you gods drink the nectar, even after the kālakūṭa poison has been swallowed, then your state as <s>Śiva</s> is certain.
Thus.
Having attained his state through the favor of the venerable <s>Yogeśvarācārya</s>,
<s>Vāmadeva</s> composed this Inquiry into Birth and Death.

children.text: abhinavamadamantharā puraṃdhrī madhusamaye madhurāś ca gītibandhāḥ
children.translated_text: Women made languid by fresh passion in springtime, and sweet compositions of song,

children.text: bata bata hṛdayaṃ haranti vāco lalitapadāś ca rahasyavastugarbhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: alas, alas, steal the heart, as do words with graceful phrases and pregnant with secret realities.
A work of the illustrious great Māheśvara teacher, the venerable Bhaṭṭa <s>Vāmadeva</s>.
When, by the course of time, decline had come upon the assembly of learned masters of texts in the refuge of true sciences,
for the practice of action, by one endowed with the vigor of good discernment wholly intent on raising up those several true dharmas

children.text: śrīmatkaśmīrādhirājena mukhyair dharmodyuktair mantribhiḥ svair vivecya ||
children.translated_text: After deliberation by the illustrious overlord of <s>Kaśmīra</s>, together with his own chief ministers intent on <s>dharma</s>,
a chief office was established there for the recovery of books pregnant with knowledge and discriminating insight.
There, by good men serving for life under the superintendence of <s>Mukundarāma</s>, this

children.text: pūrtyā śuddhyā vyākhyayā saṃskṛtaḥ stāt pūrṇo granthaḥ śreyase sajjanānām ||
children.translated_text: complete book, corrected through completion, purification, and commentary, may be for the welfare of good people.
<s>Tilaka</s>.
May it become an offering to <s>Śaṃkara</s>, whose body is the nectar of the consciousness of the blessed Self.
